wrong: args[0] can always be read. | right: If you run the program without typing the command-line argument it expects, reading args[0] fails with java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: 0.
wrong: The first command-line argument is args[1]. | right: Counting starts at 0: the first argument is args[0], the second args[1].

[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday/maths reading: '1234' typed on the command line is a number, and the first item in a list is item 1. Java rule: every command-line argument arrives as a String in args, and the first is args[0].
[1] misconception (M) -> ArgsAreNumbers: wrong rule: Command-line arguments arrive already typed as numbers, so no parsing is needed. Right rule: args[0] is always a String, so Integer.parseInt(args[0]) is needed to get its number.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> ArgsAreNumbers: Applies the args rule unevenly: maps the first typed word to args[0] on one run but to args[1] on another, or treats a numeric argument as a String in one place and as an int in another. (here mixing in: "command-line args arrive already typed, no parsing needed")

[0] names_the_element (N): Command-line arguments are the strings typed after the class name in java Name a b c; they reach main as the String array args.
[1] states_the_rule (S): args[0] represents the first string typed on the command line, args[1] the second, and so on (counting starts at 0); every element is a String.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): At launch the JVM splits the words after java Name at spaces, stores them in order in args, then calls main(args); the program reads args[k] whenever that expression is evaluated.
[1] output_prediction (OP): args[k] evaluates to the k-th typed string, e.g. java UseArgument Alice gives args[0] = "Alice" and prints Hi, Alice. How are you?
[2] one_step_execution (OS): Reading args[k] changes nothing; args is set once at launch and the same program gives different outputs only because different arguments were typed.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): args[k] is always a String, so Integer.parseInt(args[k]) or Double.parseDouble(args[k]) must convert it before arithmetic.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): The arguments arrive in main's parameter args (String[] args).
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): args.length is the number of arguments typed (0 if none), so valid indices are 0 to args.length-1.
[3] relation_to_neighbour (R): In the black-box view the command-line argument is the input string and what the program prints is the output string.
[4] relation_to_neighbour (R): Command-line arguments are a fixed number of strings given once when the program starts (args[]); standard input is a stream of any length read while the program runs (StdIn.readInt()). Both arrive as text and must be parsed into numbers.
[5] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Purpose: give the program its input at launch so the same compiled program can be tailored to different data without editing or recompiling.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> ArgsAreNumbers: Changing the typed arguments changes the output but not the program; typing fewer arguments than the program reads causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; extra arguments are ignored unless read.
[1] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Counting starts at 0: the first argument is args[0]. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: using args[1] for the first argument: wrong argument used, or ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: 1 if only one was typed
[2] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use command-line arguments for a few small inputs known at launch (sizes, names, seeds); use standard input for long or interactive input.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: args[k] exists only if at least k+1 arguments were typed. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: running without the expected argument: java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: 0
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Arguments are Strings; numbers must be parsed. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: int n = args[0]; incompatible types: String cannot be converted to int
[5] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Integer.parseInt needs digits. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: java Prog five or 12.2 where an int is parsed: NumberFormatException

wrong: If a number is typed when the program is launched, args[0] is already an int and can be used in arithmetic. | right: args[0] is always a String, so Integer.parseInt(args[0]) is needed to get its number.

Command-line arguments are a fixed number of strings given once when the program starts (args[]); standard input is a stream of any length read while the program runs (StdIn.readInt()). Both arrive as text and must be parsed into numbers.
args is the array of command-line arguments.
The black-box view treats the command-line argument as the input string and what the program prints as the output string.
args[k] is always a String, so Integer.parseInt(args[k]) is needed before it can be used as a number.
The command-line arguments arrive in main's parameter args, an array of Strings.
